entries.clue: Marvel race film remade without female (7)

indicatorNotes.remade: a film that is remade is put together again in a new form, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order
indicatorNotes.without: the fodder goes without something, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: the letters of race film with the F taken out

annotation.surface: A superhero studio remakes an old racing picture and drops its heroine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Marvel' dresses as the film studio, which suits the talk of remakes, but here it is the plain noun: a wonder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a marvel is something wonderful that cannot be explained, which is what a miracle is.

entries.clue: Abysmal ice-cream containing venom (6)

indicatorNotes.containing: the words before it contain the answer, holding it inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of abysmal into the start of ice

annotation.surface: A complaint that a dessert is so bad it might as well be poisoned.
annotation.walkthrough: The hyphen and the word break are both ignored: the hidden answer straddles 'abysmal' and 'ice'.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: venom is not only snake poison but also bitter spite, and spite is malice.

entries.clue: Wandered around with setter getting in way (6)

indicatorNotes.getting in: the setter is getting in the way, so it goes inside the word for way

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself as ME

annotation.surface: Someone wandered about while the crossword setter kept getting under their feet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Setter' giving ME is a standard convention: the compiler speaking of himself.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to roam is to move about with no fixed aim, which is wandering around.

entries.clue: Take away finest coca concoction (10)

indicatorNotes.concoction: a concoction is a mixture of ingredients, so the letters are mixed up

annotation.surface: An order at a takeaway for the best cola brew going.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take away' looks like a food order, but it is a verb meaning to remove.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym with an official edge: a teacher or customs officer who confiscates something removes it by authority.

entries.clue: Lament missing first bird (5)

indicatorNotes.missing first: the word is missing its first letter, so the opening letter goes

blocks.note: regret = lament, without its opening R

annotation.surface: Someone mourns the loss of the first bird of the season.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Missing first' reads as describing the bird, but it tells you to cut the first letter of the word before it.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: an egret is a white heron, one kind of wading bird.

entries.clue: Lays on international male models (7)

annotation.surface: An international agency supplies male models for a show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Models' looks like a noun, the fashion kind, but it is the verb: POSES.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to lay a burden or tax on someone is to impose it on them.

entries.clue: Popular coin I have as bribe (9)

annotation.surface: Someone boasts of the coin they have to slip an official.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in I'VE is dropped, as crosswords always ignore punctuation in the grid.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: a bribe is a crooked kind of inducement, and an inducement to act is an incentive.

entries.clue: Boat stake (4)

blocks.note: a flat-bottomed river boat pushed along with a pole

annotation.surface: A boat moored to a stake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stake' sits beside 'boat' as if it were a mooring post, but it is money wagered; in Britain a punter is a gambler.
annotation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses: the Cambridge-style flat river boat, and a bet, as in 'have a punt on the horses'.

entries.clue: General cleaning up (8)

blocks.note: wide-ranging, as of a statement that ignores exceptions
brushing a floor clean with a broom

annotation.surface: An army general doing the tidying.
annotation.walkthrough: 'General' poses as a military rank; it is the adjective, as in a sweeping statement.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a sweeping generalisation is broad and general, and sweeping with a broom is cleaning up.

entries.clue: President taking drug foolishly ran (8)

indicatorNotes.taking: taking something from a word removes it, so the drug comes out
indicatorNotes.foolishly: something done foolishly is done in a muddled way, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: the letters of president with one E taken out

annotation.surface: A head of state on drugs bolts off in a panic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taking' suggests swallowing the drug, but here it means taking E away.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by degree: to sprint is to run at full speed, so ran covers it.

entries.clue: Be informed of incline around start of road (5)

indicatorNotes.around: the incline goes around the letter, enclosing it
indicatorNotes.start of: the start of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A notice at the foot of a steep lane.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Incline' looks like a slope, but it is the verb: to lean.
annotation.definitionFit: Phrasal sense: to learn of news is to be told it, not to study it.

entries.clue: Story teller and traitor carrying prisoner to Europe (9)

indicatorNotes.carrying: the traitor carries the prisoner, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.to: added to, so Europe follows on at the end

annotation.surface: A treacherous guard spins a tale while escorting a prisoner to the Continent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Story teller' in this company sounds like a liar; the answer is simply someone good at telling anecdotes.
annotation.definitionFit: A French borrowing: a raconteur is a person admired for telling stories well.

entries.clue: So exciting newly living together (10)

indicatorNotes.newly: newly means made anew, so the letters are made into something new

annotation.surface: A couple gushing about having just moved in together.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a young couple's excitement, and the answer describes exactly their situation.
annotation.definitionFit: Literal build: co- (together) plus existing (living).

entries.clue: Fix options regularly (3)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of options

annotation.surface: A plea to settle on the choices available.
annotation.walkthrough: Start from the second letter of 'options' and take every other one.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to fix a notice to a board is to pin it.

entries.clue: Draw with time and revolutionary skill during battle (10)

indicatorNotes.revolutionary: a revolution turns something round, so the word is written backwards
indicatorNotes.during: during the battle means inside it, so these letters go into the word

blocks.note: action = battle, opened after the A

annotation.surface: A battle ended in a draw thanks to time and a rebel's skill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests a tied result, fitting the battle, but it is the noun meaning a pull or lure.
annotation.definitionFit: Noun sense: a star act is a big draw, something that pulls crowds in.

entries.clue: Someone you know dancing a quiet can-can (12)

indicatorNotes.dancing: dancers move about and change places, so the letters do too

annotation.surface: A friend performing an unusually subdued can-can.
annotation.walkthrough: A quiet can-can is absurd, since the dance is famously loud and high-kicking; the absurdity hides the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: someone you know, but not well enough to call a friend.

entries.clue: United nations operation put forward without dissent (9)

blocks.note: to pose a question is to put it forward

annotation.surface: A UN mission is proposed and nobody objects.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a diplomatic vote, and the answer is how such a resolution passes.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a motion that meets no dissent passes with nobody opposing it.

entries.clue: Her plans going to pieces (8)

indicatorNotes.going to: going to pieces means falling apart, so the letters fall apart and regroup

annotation.surface: Her plans are falling apart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Going to pieces' reads as one idiom; the setter splits it, so 'going to' mixes the letters and 'pieces' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: shrapnel is the jagged pieces of metal thrown out when a shell bursts.

entries.clue: Lightly fry radish tip with new English wine (8)

indicatorNotes.tip: the tip of the radish is its first letter

blocks.note: to saute is to fry lightly

annotation.surface: A recipe: saute the radish tops and serve with English wine.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a recipe, which keeps the French wine out of view until the last word.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: Sauterne, more often spelt Sauternes, is a sweet white Bordeaux wine.

entries.clue: Intimate interaction from one card to another (5-2-5)

blocks.note: a card of the red suit with a heart symbol
another card of the same suit

annotation.surface: Cards passed from one hand to another during an intimate moment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From' is only a link: the phrase from one card to another reads as the same card, TO, the same card again.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a candid private talk where both people open up about their feelings.

entries.clue: Loudly frolic and take a chance (6)

indicatorNotes.Loudly: said out loud, so it is the sound of the word that counts, not its spelling

blocks.note: to gambol is to frolic, skipping about like a lamb

annotation.surface: Someone told to frolic noisily and risk it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loudly' sits beside 'frolic' as if describing it, but it signals a sound-alike.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: betting on an uncertain outcome is taking a chance.

entries.clue: Puts off those discussing dropping degree (6)

indicatorNotes.dropping: the word is dropping something, so those letters fall out

blocks.note: debaters = those discussing, with BA (a Bachelor of Arts degree) taken out

annotation.surface: A panel of speakers is put off by talk of cutting a degree course.
annotation.walkthrough: BA, the Bachelor of Arts, is the usual degree to remove.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to discourage someone from acting is to put them off.

entries.clue: Worker accepts new technology at first (3)

indicatorNotes.at first: what comes at first in each word is its opening letter

annotation.surface: An employee embraces the latest technology from the start.
annotation.walkthrough: The ant is the crossword's standard worker; 'at first' applies to all three words before it.
annotation.definitionFit: Crossword stock: worker ants are the non-breeding labourers of the colony.

entries.clue: Be aware of ice parapet melting (10)

indicatorNotes.melting: something melting loses its shape and sets in a new one, as the letters do

annotation.surface: A warning to watch out for an icy wall that is thawing.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a safety warning, and 'Be aware of' is exactly what it asks.
annotation.definitionFit: Secondary sense: besides valuing something, to appreciate a problem is to recognise it fully.

entries.clue: Lie about one exam (5)

indicatorNotes.about: the lie goes about the one, surrounding it

annotation.surface: A student lies about one exam.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lie' suggests a fib to fit the exam story; it means lie down, REST. A resit, a British term, is an exam taken again after failing.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a resit is a particular kind of exam, the second attempt.

entries.clue: Upset keen female performer (4)

indicatorNotes.Upset: set upside down; in a down clue the word reads upwards

annotation.surface: An eager star gets upset.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like an emotional state, which suits a star's reputation, but it turns the word over in this down clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the word first meant a celebrated female opera singer.

entries.clue: Plant US drugs agent is starting to share with us (9)

indicatorNotes.starting to: the word that is starting gives only its start, the first letter

blocks.note: a narc is an American narcotics officer

annotation.surface: An undercover narcotics officer is beginning to open up to the team.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as an undercover agent, fitting the drugs story, but it is the flower.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the genus that includes daffodils and jonquils.

entries.clue: Inspire hearts of grimly robust men (5)

indicatorNotes.hearts of: the heart of a word is its middle, so take the centre letters

annotation.surface: A rallying call to stir the hearts of tough, grim men.
annotation.walkthrough: An even-length word has a two-letter heart, so the answer takes two, two and one.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: to fill someone with a feeling, as in imbued with courage, is to inspire them.

entries.clue: Sketch fish returning in direction of shelter (7)

indicatorNotes.returning: coming back the way it went, so the whole is written backwards

annotation.surface: An artist sketches a fish swimming back toward cover.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Returning' covers the whole of DRAW plus EEL, not just the fish.
annotation.definitionFit: Nautical term: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind, and leeward points that way.

entries.clue: Let nuns broadcast passages (7)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: broadcast first meant scattered widely, like sown seed, so the letters are scattered

annotation.surface: Allow the nuns to read scripture on the radio.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passages' suggests readings from a text, fitting the nuns, but they are ways through underground.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a tunnel is one kind of passage, cut underground.
